caption: A pendulum clock swings in front of a hallway mirror, and the reflected pendulum swings in time with it, mirrored.

sa.check: A pendulum clock swings in front of a hallway mirror.
The reflected pendulum swings in time with it.

pc.expect: The reflected swing is simultaneous with the real one and stops when the pendulum stops.
pc.fail: It swings out of time; or it swings while the pendulum hangs still; or it stops while the pendulum swings.

pc.expect: The reflection is a mirror image: the pendulum's swing to one side of the frame appears on the same side in the mirror.
pc.fail: The reflected swing is on the other side of the frame, as in a rotated copy; or the reflection is upside down; or it shows a different clock.

pc.expect: The reflection does not move on its own.
pc.fail: It shifts or turns while the clock is still; or slides across the mirror with nothing moving.

pc.expect: The mirror is flat and rigid: the reflection is undistorted.
pc.fail: The surface ripples; or the reflection warps; or the mirror bends.

pc.expect: One clock and one reflection; the reflection stays in the mirror.
pc.fail: A second clock appears; or the reflection leaves the mirror; or the pendulum vanishes; or the clock passes into the glass.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The clock, the mirror frame and the hallway stay the same.
pc.fail: The clock changes colour; or the frame changes; or the hallway rearranges.

note: Mirror geometry: each point of the image lies directly across the mirror surface from the real point, so the image is a mirror copy, not a rotated one.
